_description: Caddy web server / reverse proxy: automatic HTTPS, persistent certificate storage, and a PHP-FPM pairing ready to uncomment.
_comment: A RECIPE: `uxc deploy caddy` pulls the image, creates /srv/caddy, writes a starting Caddyfile, and registers the volumes + health check. Edit /srv/caddy/Caddyfile (set your domain and e-mail), then `uxc start caddy`. Upgrades follow the 2-alpine tag: `uxc upgrade caddy` re-pulls, health-gates the restart and rolls back to .prev if the new version does not come up.

_source._comment_image: The official image. A major-version tag (not :latest) so an upgrade is a patch/minor move, never a surprise jump to Caddy 3.

_comment_paths: Created before the first start, so the container never fails on a missing bind source. /srv/caddy/storage holds the ACME account key and the issued certificates - back THAT up, or every redeploy re-issues certificates and eventually hits Let's Encrypt rate limits.
_comment_seed: Written only when the file does not exist - your edited Caddyfile is never touched by a redeploy or an upgrade. The :80 health endpoint is what uxcd's health check hits, and what makes a safe upgrade able to verify the new version.

/srv/caddy/Caddyfile: # Starting Caddyfile written by `uxc deploy caddy`. EDIT ME.
# 1. replace example.org with your domain and set a real e-mail address
# 2. point DNS at this box and open 80/443 in the firewall (fw4 owns that,
# Certificates live in /var/storage (-> /srv/caddy/storage) so they survive
# Health endpoint on plain HTTP: uxcd's health check and the safe-upgrade
# gate use this. Keep it, or the upgrade cannot verify a new version.
# PHP? deploy the php-fpm recipe too and uncomment this line. Both
# containers must share a network - the host stack (the default) or one

_comment_registry: The uxcd half: binds, health check, web links. Only keys the entry does not already have are written, so your edits survive every redeploy and upgrade.

_registry.notes: Deployed from the 'caddy' recipe. Config: /srv/caddy/Caddyfile (bind-mounted read-only; `uxc restart caddy` to apply). ACME certificates and the account key live in /srv/caddy/storage - back it up; losing it re-issues everything. The health check needs the :80 /healthz block in the Caddyfile. For a PHP site, deploy the php-fpm recipe and uncomment php_fastcgi 127.0.0.1:9000; the two containers must share a network (host, or the same --infra netns).
